title: Waiting out the uncertainty
request:
A clock uncertain by ±5, and one transaction committing

./your_program.sh commit-wait
init 5
now
commit t1
state
note: The transaction is done well before it is announced. That gap is the price of being able to compare timestamps across machines that have never spoken to each other — and it is why the engineering effort goes into shrinking ε with GPS and atomic clocks rather than into the algorithm.

title: The same two commits without the wait
request:
Two transactions committing back to back with commit-wait disabled

./your_program.sh commit-wait
init 5
commit-wait off
commit t1
commit t2
external-order
note: t2 began after t1 had finished, and their timestamps say they are simultaneous. Nothing inside the system notices; an observer who watched t1 commit and then started t2 sees a database that disagrees with the order they watched happen.
